About.Heading: About me
Paragraphs: I'm a full-stack developer with a focus on .NET and modern JavaScript. I started out maintaining an internal inventory system, which taught me more about schema design and error handling than any tutorial — mainly because I broke it a few times first.

My coding philosophy is boring on purpose: name things clearly, keep side effects where a reader expects them, and write the test that reproduces the bug before fixing it. I'd rather ship something a teammate can change at 2am than something clever nobody can read.

What drives me is the gap between a working prototype and a system people actually trust. I like the unglamorous part — the loading states, the validation messages, the indexes that make a slow page feel instant.

Projects.Title: Client portal with white-label theming
Projects.Summary: A multi-tenant portal serving 11 client brands from one deployment. Each tenant supplies its own logo, palette and copy through configuration rather than a code branch.
Challenges: Replaced an app-per-client deployment with a single build where branding is entirely configuration-driven, cutting release work from a day to minutes.
Kept tenant assets isolated — a bad logo path degrades to a text mark instead of a broken layout.
Moved document generation off the request thread so 200-page reports no longer time out.

Projects.Title: Inventory reconciliation service
Projects.Summary: Background service reconciling warehouse stock counts against sales and purchase records, flagging discrepancies for review instead of silently overwriting them.
Challenges: Made the reconciliation idempotent so a restart mid-run cannot double-adjust stock.
Tuned the diff query from 90 seconds to under 2 with a covering index and a set-based merge.
Built an audit trail that answers 'why did this count change' months later.

Projects.Title: CSV import pipeline for messy spreadsheets
Projects.Summary: Self-service import tool letting operations staff load supplier spreadsheets with inconsistent headers, encodings and date formats — without a developer present.
Challenges: Column mapping learned from the header row, so renamed columns do not break the import.
Row-level validation reports every problem at once rather than failing on the first.
Streamed the parse so a 400k-row file uses flat memory.

Projects.Title: Real-time ops dashboard
Projects.Summary: Live floor dashboard showing machine status and queue depth, replacing a whiteboard plus a spreadsheet refreshed every shift.
Challenges: Pushed updates over SignalR with automatic reconnect so a dropped tablet reconnects without a reload.
Collapsed per-machine event streams into 1-second aggregates to keep payloads small.
Designed for a 1024×600 kiosk screen readable from three metres away.

Projects.Title: Open-source: MySQL index analyzer
Projects.Summary: A small CLI that reads EF Core's generated SQL and suggests the indexes a MySQL schema is missing. Used by my own team on three production systems.
Challenges: Parsed the query tree just far enough to find predicate columns without reimplementing a SQL parser.
Kept suggestions conservative — it proposes, it never applies DDL.

Projects.Title: Booking flow revamp
Projects.Summary: Rebuilt a four-step booking journey that had a 38% abandonment at step two, reducing it to two steps with inline validation.
Challenges: Instrumented each step to find the real drop-off instead of guessing from complaints.
Preserved in-progress bookings across sessions so a closed tab was not a lost booking.
Cut abandonment at the previously worst step from 38% to 11%.
